rows.why: Two short heavily-ionising prongs stop away from 18001 (18025 -> 18026 at 152-160k and 18003 -> 18006 rising to ~180k) while the only 'rises TOWARD' vote, seg 18021, is a 285k single-point spike inside 1 cm that crashes to ~50k and stays flat for 9 cm - a vertex blob, not a Bragg rise - so the shower apex 18023 10 cm up the stem is downstream of the real hadronic vertex.

Seg 9039 shows a textbook monotone rise over its last ~8 cm tracking the stopping-muon template up to 165k at 9022, with a 12.6 cm MIP tail (9031+9040) hanging off that same end - a Michel, so 9022 is the far end (rule 3) - and the muon's other end 9006 is a near-90-degree kink where the rest of the event (shower chain 9014/9012/9019...) departs, and it is also the lowest-z candidate.

The 126 cm track Bragg-peaks at 7000 (175k falling to MIP within 8 cm) so it starts at 7001, and 7001 is exactly where a 290k point-like deposit sits and where a fan of small fragment clusters (49, 50, 28, 55) begins - the intermediate 7002 is only a 12-degree kink with MIP dQ/dx on both sides and cannot be a vertex.

The only structure in the event is a deg-3 junction at 8001 from which an 11.5 cm proton rises monotonically 130k -> 205k and stops at 8000, plus a 1.7 cm 167k pi+ stub and a 3 cm MIP stub - everything comes out of 8001.

21003 is the single 48-degree junction of the event: a 29.6 cm heavily-ionising prong leaves it and Bragg-peaks to 250k at 21001 following the proton template, while the 175 cm muon leaves the other way and stops at 21000 with a 6.5 cm MIP fragment (cluster 61) 1.7 cm off its end - a Michel, so 21000 is the far end.

Seg 15004 rises smoothly 90k -> 305k along the brown proton template and stops at 15001, so it emanates from 15003, which is also where the 132.7 cm flat-MIP muon starts before exiting the detector bottom at y = -195.

31036 is the junction of two heavy prongs, one of which (31028, 12.8 cm) starts at the ~75k expected for a proton of that residual range and Bragg-peaks to 305k at 31034; the 46 cm MIP chain of cluster 6 extrapolates backwards to within ~3 cm of 31036, and 31036 is the lowest-z candidate of the whole corner activity.

The geometric inverted-V apex near (z~139, y~-89) is rejected because both arms' hot ends face it (6004 rises smoothly to a stopping peak at 6001, 74030 is hot at 74032) and no vertex can emit two prongs that Bragg inward, leaving 6003 as the only multi-prong candidate with an away-vote and no toward-vote, corroborated by cluster 75's axis back-extrapolating to y = -114.6, exactly 6003's y - though the event is fragmented into three separated pieces and I am not far from guessing.

The 202 cm muon has its end deposit at 11000 (155k falling to MIP over ~10 cm, following the templates) so it starts at 11001, where a 0.7 cm proton stub is attached and a diffuse cloud of sub-cm fragments (clusters 38, 40, 41, 42) sits 17-38 cm away; my only reservation is that z = 8.4 cm is close enough to the upstream face that the track could have entered rather than started.

16003 is a degree-5 junction carrying three short heavily-ionising proton stubs (167k, 159k->187k, 82k) plus an 81 cm prong that leaves at a sub-MIP 30450 and rises 5x to 152k where it stops at 16000 - every attached prong gets hotter away from 16003.

Rule 1 fully satisfied at the only real cluster: 15002 is the deg-2 junction between two Bragg ends (52.8 cm muon rising 53k->128k into 15000, 9.1 cm proton stub hot at 15003), and the zoom shows both attached segments as green arrows.

Rule 7 apex: in X-Z the whole 342 cm shower opens as a clean V whose apex is 23009 at the lowest z (426 cm), with two ~24 cm prongs getting hotter away and a 2.1 cm 151k e/cm recoil stub sitting on the apex itself; downgraded from certain because the prongs could be hadronic (rule 4).

Rule 1 textbook: 3 of 4 segments rise away from 3011 - a 190 cm muon with a clean template-following Bragg at 3000, a 28.7 cm proton rising monotonically 35k->230k into 3007, and a pion that stops at 3004 where it makes a secondary star of short hot stubs.

The event is a single 15.7 cm flat-MIP segment with no dQ/dx gradient at either end, so the only real discriminator is that the 18000 end sits at y=-198.0 against the -200 wall and must be an exit/entry, leaving 18001 as the only end that can be an origin.

Classic two-Bragg-ends trap resolved by rule 1: both prongs rise away from the deg-2 junction 3002 (46.3 cm arm climbing the muon template to 210k at 3001, 17.7 cm arm reaching 240k at 3000), so 3002 is the point they both point away from.

12003 is the deg-2 junction where an 89 cm muon leaves and Braggs at 12001 while a 7 cm proton stub Braggs at its free end 12000; only 1 of 2 formally rises away and the muon carries a hot spike at the 12003 end itself, so the junction wins but less cleanly than the other two-prong events.

Rule 8 abstention: cluster 6 is a single 21 cm curled MIP squiggle with no Bragg anywhere and both free ends (6006, 6000) reading red/flat, and its only apex-like point - the 6005/6003 hairpin - lies at y=199.4 against the 200 cm top wall, so there is no contained origin to name.

Rule 1 with both prongs measured: from 6002 a 104 cm muon runs flat at MIP and Braggs to 125k at 6001 while a 36.1 cm proton falls monotonically from 330k at 6000 back to 90k at 6002, so both stop away from 6002.

All three attached segments show green arrows at the deg-3 junction 3004 - a 6.3 cm stub climbing 39k->110k into 3001, a 5.8 cm prong rising to 79k at 3005, and a 19 cm MIP track running off to 3003 - the complete everything-comes-out-of-the-vertex signature.
Both arms of the 90 cm cluster Bragg away from the deg-2 junction 18002: a 45.2 cm proton on the proton template reaching 220k at 18000 and a 44.3 cm muon flat at MIP then rising to 205k at 18001.
